_instructions: Measured CXT layout: 5 rows x 4 columns, plus 4 knobs. Find keys by physical position, top to bottom and left to right: key caps may show something else. USB interface 0 must already use WinUSB. This map does not reprogram the keyboard.
Row 1: E -> slot 1 | B -> slot 2 | Ctrl+Z -> slot 3 | Space -> interrupt.
Row 2: G -> approve | Ctrl+F -> deny | hold H -> voice_down, release H -> voice_up | Alt -> modifier-only, unbound (sends no letter).
Row 3: L -> screenshot | M -> prompt continue | Ctrl+T -> prompt tests | Ctrl+D -> prompt summary (bound, dangerous under Raw Input: two presses exit Claude Code).
Row 4: Ctrl -> modifier-only, unbound | Shift -> modifier-only, unbound | U -> prompt commit | X -> cycle +1.
Row 5: Tab -> next_wait | Ctrl+C -> unbound (dangerous under Raw Input: interrupt / exit) | Ctrl+V -> unbound (dangerous under Raw Input: paste) | P -> cycle -1.
Knob 1 clockwise F (hid:0x09) -> app next (next session inside Claude desktop), counterclockwise S (hid:0x16) -> app prev; neither changes the selected overlay slot. Press L (hid:0x0F) -> screenshot.
Knob 2 clockwise R -> cycle +1, counterclockwise P -> cycle -1, press Q -> show (un-hide the overlay; no mouse needed).

Knob 3 clockwise - -> scroll 1 (wheel down over the selected agent window, toward newer text), counterclockwise = -> scroll -1 (up); direction not yet verified (one - detent captured). Press V (hid:0x19) -> scroll end (to the bottom).

Knob 4 clockwise ] -> nav down, counterclockwise [ -> nav up (rotation not yet verified; only [ seen once; arrow keys only while the agent asks a question), press C (hid:0x06) -> nav enter (Enter; sends dictated text). nav is refused while a permission request is open: use approve/deny.

Raw Input (interface 0 still on the system HID driver): every key also types into the focused window, so app, prompt, nav, voice and screenshot are refused until interface 0 uses WinUSB. Dangerous leaks: Ctrl+D (two presses exit Claude Code), Ctrl+C (interrupt / exit), Ctrl+V (paste).
Slots 4..6 are available through HTTP or custom bindings. Only fresh single-key presses with exact device modifiers trigger actions. High-risk approvals need two presses within 1.5 seconds.

A string binding runs on key down. An object can bind down and up separately; up pairs with the accepted physical press even if modifiers change. Voice guards last at most 60 seconds; approvals and other window/input actions require releasing voice first.
Opt in with hub.py --backend usb --profile v2_emulation. The top-level default bindings stay unchanged. Physical codes below come from measured pc/deck_map.json; no keyboard reprogramming.
Slots 1..6: E, B, factory Ctrl+Z, Space, knob 2 press Q, knob 3 press V. G approves, factory Ctrl+F denies, hold H starts voice and release H stops it; knob 1 press L captures a screenshot.
All four knobs cycle sessions on rotation. Knob 4 press factory Ctrl+0 is the confirmed alternate interrupt key.

Four additional Ctrl+session prompt bindings are logical chords over known usages, pending a physical report capture. Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V remain unbound in every profile. The main PC keyboard Ctrl does not modify this USB device.

Factory Ctrl+Z already contains Ctrl, so Ctrl+slot 3 cannot be distinguished from slot 3. Factory Ctrl+F already contains Ctrl, so Ctrl+deny cannot be distinguished from deny. These two requested physical chords are pending an independently confirmed key; no guessed binding is installed.
Ctrl macros are decoded modifier-first: a Ctrl-only report then the main-key report. Fresh modifiers last until consumed by a main key. See hub_keys.md for labels and confirmation gaps.
